reviews.explanation: The mention 元凱 is the courtesy name of 杜預 (Du Yu). The Liu annotation sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-012-liu-annotation-001 explicitly states '元凱京兆杜陵人' and '王隱晉書曰預字', directly identifying 元凱 as 杜預. The main text also refers to 杜預 in the same story context. The annotation evidence specifically supports the identity resolution.

The mention 預 is the personal name of 杜預. The Liu annotation sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-012-liu-annotation-003 describes his offices (都督荆州諸軍事, 鎮襄陽, 封當陽侯, 累遷河南尹, 鎮南將軍), which match the biography of 杜預. The annotation evidence specifically identifies this person as 杜預.

The mention 預 in the annotation '王隱晉書曰預字' refers to 杜預 by personal name. The annotation sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-012-liu-annotation-001 explicitly states '王隱晉書曰預字' and '元凱京兆杜陵人', directly linking 預 to 元凱 and to 杜預. The annotation evidence specifically supports this identity.

The mention 和長輿 appears in the main text of story 05-fangzheng-012. 和長輿 is the surname-plus-courtesy-name form for 和嶠 (He Jiao). The main text context describes him arriving at a gathering where 杜預 is being seen off, and the story's narrative context supports this identification. The main text evidence sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-012-main contains the mention and provides the contextual role match. While the reference semantics record is marked 'uncertain' (fail closed), the main text evidence does specifically contain the surface form 和長輿, which is a well-attested alias for 和嶠, and the contextual role (a prominent figure at the farewell gathering) is consistent with 和嶠's historical standing.

The mention 王隱 appears in the Liu annotation as '王隱晉書曰預字' — explicitly identifying 王隱 as the author of the 晉書 being cited. The annotation directly attributes the statement about 預's courtesy name 元凱 to 王隱's 晉書. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-a4735dd3b5073db174f4) provides the canonical name 王隱. The source explicitly names 王隱 as the author of the cited work, which is a direct identification. The distinctness from Du Yu and other figures is also clear from context.

The mention 杜預 appears in the main text as the opening subject: '杜預之荆州頓七里橋'. The Liu annotations explicitly identify this figure: annotation 001 states '元凱京兆杜陵人' and '王隱晉書曰預字', annotation 002 gives his biography as 荆州刺史 with lineage from 御史大夫延年, and annotation 003 describes him as 鎮南將軍 who 封當陽侯. These annotations directly identify the 杜預 in the main text as Du Yu, the Jin dynasty general and scholar. The candidate evidence provides the canonical name 杜預. The identity is explicitly supported by the source annotations.

The mention 預 (with courtesy name 元凱) is explicitly identified in the Liu annotation as 杜預. Annotation 001 states '王隱晉書曰預字' (王隱's 晉書 says 預's courtesy name is...), and annotation 002 provides his biography: 荆州刺史, 漢御史大夫延年十一世孫, 祖畿魏太保, 父恕幽州(刺史). These biographical details match the candidate 杜預. The alias registry evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-6185ae1f895c1a9ac387) confirms 元凱 as 杜預's courtesy name. The coreference with other mentions of 杜預 in the text is consistent.

The mention 長輿 appears in the main text: '須臾和長輿來問楊右衛何在'. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-04e4204a858ac8ae5b66) from the alias registry explicitly states '和嶠字長輿' — 和嶠's courtesy name is 長輿. The main text uses the full name '和長輿', which combines the surname 和 with the courtesy name 長輿, directly matching the alias registry entry. The context (a Jin dynasty anecdote about 杜預 and court figures) is consistent with 和嶠 being a Jin official. The alias registry explicitly identifies 長輿 as 和嶠's courtesy name, and the main text's '和長輿' directly combines surname + courtesy name, providing explicit identification.

assertions.interpretation: The scene is set at the time when Du Yu was going to Jingzhou (as governor).
At that time, all court officials gathered to see him off at Qili Bridge.
Background: He was not well regarded by others (in his youth), prior to the scene.

assertions.interpretation: At the farewell gathering, Yang Ji, being a famous and outstanding figure, could not bear it and left without sitting down.

assertions.interpretation: The guest reports that Yang Ji had just left without sitting, referring to the immediately preceding moment.
He went to Daxia Gate and indeed found Yang Ji reviewing cavalry there, a subsequent event in the scene.
Later outcome: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dangyang for his merit in pacifying Wu, after the scene.
Later outcome: He was posthumously granted the title of General of the South with the honor of Yitong Sansi, after his death.
